o: Rose a little higher and his
questions.s: 'Coldest' is a superlative and may not be appropriate without a clear comparison. 'Cold' is more suitable for a state.

questions.q: This is most expensive car in the showroom.
questions.s:
The sentence contains an error. The correct usage is to include "the" before the superlative adjective "most."

The corrected sentence would be: “This is the most expensive car in the showroom.”

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

She is the least reliablest person of all.
questions.s: The most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment is 'least reliable'. 'Least reliablest' is not correct because "least" is already a superlative form indicating the lowest degree of reliability. Adding "-est" to "reliable" is redundant and incorrect. "Least reliable" is the correct form that indicates that the person is the most unreliable out of all possible options, which aligns with the intended meaning of the sentence. Option (a) is grammatically incorrect. "Leastest" is not a standard English word, and it doesn't follow the pattern of forming superlatives. Therefore, it is not the correct choice. Option (b) is not correct because this option does not accurately convey the intended meaning. "Less reliable" implies that the person is not as reliable as others but it does not necessarily indicate that they are the least reliable out of all possible options. Option (d) is incorrect. "Lesser" is typically used as a comparative adjective, but in this context, a superlative form is needed. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q: On entering the crowding room (a) / I could not see one person (b)/whom I knew. (c) / No error (d)
o: I could not see one person
questions.s:
The word “crowding” is incorrect because it is a present participle, not an adjective.
The correct adjective is “crowded room.”

o: is getting more and more worse
and now we cannot do anything.
questions.s: Only "worse and worse" or "more and more bad", not both together.

questions.s: Use "than John's" or "than that of John" to compare houses.

questions.q: The vacancy was filled (1)/ by a young scholar (2)/ who had an extensible knowledge of ancient art. (3)/ No error. (4)
o: who had an extensible knowledge of ancient art.
questions.s: The correct adjective is “extensive”, meaning widespread or thorough.

questions.q:
It was a really bad movie- a worse movie I've ever seen in my life.

[CGL Tier II 13/9/2019]
questions.s: "Worst" is the superlative form, used when comparing more than two things. "Worse" is comparative, used for comparing two things. Therefore, "the worst" is correct.

questions.q: Even today / it is incredulous to think / that men have walked on the moon.
o: that men have walked on the moon.
questions.s:
Explanation:- Use incredible in place of incredulous.

incredible(positive sense)(kuchh itna achcha ya bada ho ki yakeen na ho ki ye sahi me hai):-impossible or very difficult to believe

incredulous (negative sense) (jo kisi cheez par shak kare):-not willing or not able to believe something

questions.q: The cake tastes sweetly and moistly, just like homemade.
questions.s:
The correct option is (d) "sweetly and moistly."

So, the error lies in using "sweetly" and "moistly" as adverbs instead of using the adjectives "sweet" and "moist" to modify the verb "tastes."

The correct sentence should be: "The cake tastes sweet and moist, just like homemade."

questions.q: There are many species of parakeets in India, the (recognizable) being the Rose-ringed parakeet.
questions.s: The sentence compares one species with all others in the group, so it needs a superlative adjective.

questions.q: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options.
questions.s:
Answer: most urgent

Explanation:
The correct superlative form of "urgent" is "most urgent" (सबसे आवश्यक).

  • More urgent is comparative, used when comparing two things.

  • Urgentest and urgenter are incorrect and not valid English words.

So, "most urgent" correctly replaces "urgent" to express the highest degree of concern.

lower marbles = neeche marbles (meaning less)
